fight: Can a custom EndpointDiscovery plugin be added to llm-d-router without forking the repo?

side_a.position: Yes: the plugin registry is an exported package-level map with an exported Register(); docs say register the factory before Run(); main.go is a thin wrapper over an importable runner.
claims: registry.go: Registry is an exported map[string]FactoryFunc and Register() is exported
PR #908: a custom discovery backend is enabled purely through configuration once registered
discovery.md: register the factory via fwkplugin.Register before calling Run, then reference it in EndpointPickerConfig

side_b.position: Only in-tree is supported: the official tutorial says to edit runner.go's registerInTreePlugins(); the Runner exposes no WithPlugins hook; no downstream out-of-tree example exists; duplicate type names silently overwrite.
claims: create_new_filter.md instructs adding plugin.Register inside cmd/epp/runner/runner.go
registerInTreePlugins() is unexported; no exported plugin-injection option on Runner
Register() has no duplicate-key guard

evidence_quality_delta: Both sides are empirical (source code + official docs); side A is code-level capability, side B is documentation/support posture plus an audited absence of precedent.
scope_overlap: Scoped differently, both right: out-of-tree registration is technically sound (Go init() + exported registry) but undocumented, unprecedented, and exposed to internal-API drift.

fight: How does precise prefix-cache routing receive KV events from backends that are not Kubernetes pods?

side_a.position: Router-side pull: each EPP replica opens an outbound ZMQ SUB connection to every discovered pod's PUB socket, driven by a Kubernetes pod reconciler; topic kv@<pod-ip>:<port>@<model>.
claims: precise-prefix guide: router-side subscription is connect-initiated per discovered pod
kv-cache config: default Auto-Discovery Mode is a Kubernetes pod reconciler needing pods get/list/watch RBAC

side_b.position: Push via Static Endpoint Mode: indexer binds a ZMQ SUB socket and backends connect out as PUB clients, with zero Kubernetes API access; pod identity is an opaque string.
claims: kv-cache config: Static Endpoint Mode (discoverPods: false + zmqEndpoint) requires no Kubernetes API
Valkey example: scoring API treats pod identity as an arbitrary opaque string

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical (current docs); the RH Oct-2025 'kv@pod-id@model' topic claim is stale versus HEAD's kv@IP:port@model.
scope_overlap: Both modes exist; OPEN QUESTION whether the EPP-embedded indexer in file-discovery mode can use Static Endpoint Mode (push) or needs endpoints fed from the EPP datastore — and whether identity strings line up (ip:port vs NamespacedName).

fight: Does the llm-d router lose capabilities when run with file/custom discovery instead of Kubernetes?

side_a.position: No loss of routing intelligence: scoring, filtering, picking, saturation admission, FlowControl, P/D and Prometheus metrics behave exactly as on Kubernetes.
claims: no-k8s blog: the router is platform-invariant by construction
guide: scheduling profile identical to optimized baseline
discovery.md: all scheduling, request control, and metrics collection behaviour is unchanged

side_b.position: Inputs and lifecycle are lost: InferenceObjective (priority/SLO), InferenceModelRewrite, k8s-notification-source and PodMonitor discovery are inactive; readiness gating and dead-endpoint eviction become the caller's job.
claims: file plugin README + discovery.md: InferenceModelRewrite, InferenceObjective, k8s-notification-source inactive
llm-d no-k8s doc: InferenceObjective-driven FlowControl, InferenceModelRewrite, PodMonitor discovery out of scope
blog: endpoint lifecycle removal is the orchestrator's responsibility off Kubernetes

evidence_quality_delta: Same upstream authors on both sides; empirical. Minor internal discrepancy: whether FlowControl itself or only its InferenceObjective priority input is affected.
scope_overlap: Scoped differently: routing LOGIC has parity; routing INPUTS (CRD-driven policy) and endpoint LIFECYCLE (health/eviction) do not.

fight: Should non-pod backends be made to look like Kubernetes objects (selectorless Service + EndpointSlice, virtual pods, Slurm-as-pods) so the stock InferencePool path works?

side_a.position: Viable: selectorless Service + manual EndpointSlice is the officially documented way to expose external endpoints; virtual-kubelet providers define pod IPs; Slinky runs Slurm workers as real pods; InferencePoolImport reaches other clusters.
claims: EndpointSlices doc: manual EndpointSlices for selectorless Services are the supported path
Slinky NodeSet makes Slurm workers real pods
InferencePoolImport imports remote InferencePools

side_b.position: Not viable for the EPP: InferencePool selects Pods by label only (not Services/EndpointSlices); manual EndpointSlices fail silently on port-name mismatch; interLink excludes long-running services and its Slurm plugin networking is egress-only.
claims: InferencePool represents a group of Pods selected by label
port-name mismatch installs a REJECT rule while kubectl shows healthy endpoints
interLink scopes long-running services out; Slurm plugin networking is SSH/tsocks egress

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is stronger for the EPP use case (spec-level: InferencePool selects Pods); side A is valid for plain Service routing and for the Slurm-as-real-pods inverse strategy.
scope_overlap: Partly scoped: EndpointSlice/virtual-pod shims do not reach the EPP at all; Slinky (real pods) does, but only if a Kubernetes control plane is acceptable.

fight: When the EPP is unavailable, should traffic to non-pod backends fail open or fail closed?

side_a.position: Fail-open is an established option: InferencePool endpointPickerRef.failureMode FailOpen, GIE v1.4 FailOpen, Envoy ext_proc failure_mode_allowed, kgateway static-cluster fallback.
claims: InferencePool failureMode FailOpen forwards to a gateway-chosen endpoint if the EPP fails
Envoy ext_proc exposes failure_mode_allowed telemetry

side_b.position: Standalone/non-pod routing is fail-closed by design: with passthrough there is no local endpoint list to fall back to; maintainers questioned exposing fail-open for a sidecar EPP; fail-open remains an open issue.
claims: agentgateway standalone routing deliberately fail-closed (PR #1429/#1658)
#1661 fail-open fallback for standalone EPP still open
maintainer: no separate service endpoint fallback path when EPP is a sidecar

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical/expert-opinion from maintainers; tight fight.
scope_overlap: Scoped: fail-open works where the proxy has its own endpoint set (Gateway mode); outside Kubernetes the EPP is a hard data-path dependency, so HA EPP replicas (v0.9) replace fail-open.

fight: Does llm-d/GIE 'Standalone Mode' mean running without Kubernetes?

side_a.position: Standalone is the non-Gateway path for the EPP: no InferencePool required in agentgateway standalone, standalone became the llm-d default in v0.7, GIE designed standalone for RL/batch/single-tenant workloads.
claims: agentgateway standalone mode does not support InferencePool
v0.7: standalone mode default
GIE #1838 motivating use cases RL/batch

side_b.position: Standalone still assumes Kubernetes: charts are Helm/kubectl-native, the agentgateway standalone chart still generates a k8s Service, standalone EPP depended on the InferencePool CRD, and maintainers describe it as bypassing the CRD, not Kubernetes.
claims: predicted-latency guide: standalone means no Gateway API object, not no Kubernetes
standalone agentgateway chart still generates a Kubernetes Service
llm-d-router charts expose no discovery/dataLayer knobs

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical; terminology conflict rather than factual disagreement.
scope_overlap: Terminology: Standalone = no Gateway API objects; only file/custom EndpointDiscovery removes Kubernetes itself.

fight: Is llm-d's router fundamentally Kubernetes-native, or is Kubernetes an incidental dependency?

side_a.position: Kubernetes-native at its core: founding post and maintainer talks call it k8s-native; datalayer events model Kubernetes object lifecycle; EndpointMetadata is documented as Kubernetes Pod state; identity is types.NamespacedName even in file discovery.
claims: founding post: Kubernetes-native
EndpointMetadata = the relevant Kubernetes Pod state
FileDiscovery still keys endpoints by types.NamespacedName

side_b.position: Incidental: routing intelligence never needed an API server; maintainers want K8s, file, Slurm and Ray discovery all as plugins; polling data sources and metrics scraping are address-agnostic; KV index identity is opaque.
claims: blog: the dependency on Kubernetes was incidental
PR #908: we want K8s, file, Slurm, and Ray discovery all as plugins
PollingDataSource requires only an Endpoint

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical; side A reflects historical design and residual types, side B the current direction.
scope_overlap: Temporal: k8s-native by origin, decoupling in progress; residual k8s-shaped identity types (NamespacedName, pool namespace) remain and must be synthesized by non-pod integrations.

fight: Which data-plane mechanism should honor an EPP-selected ip:port that is not a Kubernetes pod?

side_a.position: Envoy ORIGINAL_DST cluster with use_http_header on x-gateway-destination-endpoint — what llm-d's no-Kubernetes guide ships.
claims: envoy.yaml: ORIGINAL_DST + CLUSTER_PROVIDED + http_header_name x-gateway-destination-endpoint
discovery.md: Envoy ORIGINAL_DST reads the header set by the EPP

side_b.position: Alternatives: agentgateway standalone passthrough (trust EPP destination directly); Envoy override-host / dynamic_forwarding LB policy for multi-host fallback; kgateway left Envoy entirely for agentgateway.
claims: agentgateway PR #1658 destinationMode: passthrough
Envoy PR #38757 dynamic_forwarding vs setUpstreamOverrideHost debate
kgateway #11824 abandoned Envoy data plane for AI

evidence_quality_delta: Both empirical; the Envoy upstream ORIGINAL_DST README documents only the connection-level variant (documentation gap).
scope_overlap: Multiple valid mechanisms; ORIGINAL_DST+header is simplest and supported by llm-d's guide; passthrough and dynamic_forwarding differ on retry/fallback semantics.

fight: Is it worth staying on llm-d's router for non-pod backends, versus routers that are static-URL-first?

side_a.position: Alternatives are simpler and possibly faster off-Kubernetes: vLLM Router claims +25% throughput and 1.2-2 s faster TTFT than llm-d; vLLM Router, production-stack and Dynamo ship static/file discovery natively with discovery decoupled from policy.
claims: vLLM Router: 25% higher throughput, 1200 ms faster TTFT vs llm-d
vLLM Router docs are static-worker-URL-first
Dynamo file-based discovery backend

side_b.position: llm-d's plugin depth is the asset: large measured gains over round-robin, precise prefix / predicted latency / flow control / P/D profiles, and even NVIDIA Dynamo reuses the EPP for vanilla vLLM fleets; the vLLM Router comparison is vendor-internal with llm-d engineers assisting.
claims: cache-aware routing 57x faster TTFT vs round-robin (llm-d-reported)
Dynamo 'GAIE with vanilla vLLM' topology uses the EPP
vLLM Router benchmark unpublished harness

evidence_quality_delta: Both sides are vendor-reported benchmarks without independent reproduction — evidence is weak on both sides.
scope_overlap: Genuine but low-resolution disagreement; the user's stated constraint (maximize llm-d reuse) makes this a check on the premise rather than the decision.

fight: Should managed/external model APIs (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock) be routed through the llm-d EPP as another kind of non-pod backend?

side_a.position: Gateways can front both classes in one entry point: agentgateway fronts Azure OpenAI and a KAITO/EPP pool; Agent Router routes 16+ providers and InferencePools from one AIGatewayRoute.
claims: AKS: agentgateway fronts both an external managed provider and a self-hosted EPP pool
Agent Router abstracts 16+ providers

side_b.position: Not inside the EPP/InferencePool: GIE and Azure put managed providers out of scope and at a higher AI-gateway tier; AIGatewayRoute backendRefs are InferencePool OR AIServiceBackend, never mixed; plain k8s Service backends were disabled in Agent Router.
claims: Azure AGC: routing to managed provider endpoints is outside the scope
GIE api-overview: model-as-a-service integration at a higher AI Gateway layer
Agent Router #902: plain Service support deliberately disabled

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is spec-level and consistent across vendors; side A actually supports the same layered conclusion.
scope_overlap: Not a genuine disagreement: both describe a two-tier design where the gateway picks the provider class and the EPP picks within self-hosted pools.

fight: Must a non-pod backend expose metrics on the same address:port it serves inference on?

side_a.position: Yes with file discovery: metrics are scraped from the same address:port; no separate metrics endpoint per backend.
claims: FileDiscovery: metrics scraped from the same address:port that serves inference

side_b.position: No at the data-model level: EndpointMetadata.MetricsHost can differ from the inference address; metrics-data-source scrapes any address string over HTTP(S).
claims: discovery.md: MetricsHost defaults to address:port only if left empty
metrics-data-source is address-agnostic

scope_overlap: Scoped: a limitation of the file plugin's schema, not of the EPP; a custom discovery plugin can set MetricsHost.

fight: Can discovered endpoints be addressed by hostname or IPv6?

side_a.position: IPv4 literals only: file discovery rejects hostnames and IPv6 ('matching the pod discovery contract').
claims: file plugin validateIPv4Address; IPv6 not supported

side_b.position: Hostnames are allowed in the multicluster-file-discovery variant, and the address validator is injected so variants can loosen it.
claims: multicluster-file-discovery config: address may be a hostname
validator injected so a variant can loosen it

scope_overlap: Scoped: pod-level file discovery is IPv4-only; a custom plugin (or the multicluster variant's pattern) can resolve names itself before Upsert.

fight: What is the EndpointPickerConfig key that selects the discovery plugin?

side_a.position: dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef (blog, shipped no-Kubernetes guide config) or EndpointPickerConfig.discovery.pluginRef (discovery.go comment).
claims: no-k8s guide config.yaml uses dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef

side_b.position: dataLayer.discovery.endpoints.pluginRef, per PR #2434 (merged 2026-08-25) and docs/discovery.md; a migration shim still accepts the legacy form.
claims: PR #2434 consolidates discovery config under dataLayer.discovery.endpoints; migrateDiscoveryConfig honors the legacy key
runner.resolveDiscovery reads DataLayer.Discovery.Endpoints.PluginRef

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is newer code; side A is legacy-but-accepted.
scope_overlap: Resolved: use dataLayer.discovery.endpoints.pluginRef on router builds after 2026-08-25; legacy key works via shim.

fight: Should non-Kubernetes RL rollout routing use a bespoke control plane (rl-controller) or the EPP?

side_a.position: A bespoke framework-agnostic control plane (rl-controller / RolloutControl API) owning weight sync, lifecycle and routing.
claims: rl-rollout north-star proposal

side_b.position: The EPP with file/custom discovery is the recommended path; rl-controller moved to legacy with no active development.
claims: legacy/rl-controller: not the recommended starting point for new work

evidence_quality_delta: Side B is the project's own current statement.
scope_overlap: Resolved in favor of EPP-based routing.
